title: review: R20 v3: document every new scheduler, routing, allocation, strategy, speculation and promotion key in pool.toml at its in-code default
spec:
v2: the v1 spec text contained a literal double-brace placeholder that the prompt renderer rejects; this text spells it out in words instead. Why: the roadmap modules merged in this goal read their configuration from pool.toml tables with defaults in code ([scheduler] duration_*/reserve_imminent/concurrency_mode/merge_pressure_*/jev_*; [jev.routing] max_adjustment, evidence_floor_n; [jev.points]; [allocation]; [strategy]; [speculation]; [promotion]). Nothing in pool.toml shows them, so an operator cannot see what is tunable or which mode a feature runs in (brief P15/P16: configuration and activation state must be visible). 
What (config only; no Python):
1. .orchestrator/pool.toml: add the keys below with exactly the in-code defaults and a one-line comment each; behaviour must not change (a test asserts the parsed values equal the module defaults). Under the existing [scheduler] table: duration_mode = "empirical", duration_min_samples = 5, duration_trim = 0.1, reserve_imminent = true, concurrency_mode = "adaptive", merge_pressure_mode = "observe", merge_queue_elevated = 3, merge_queue_saturated = 5, merge_conflicts_saturated = 2, jev_mode = "shadow", jev_max_pairs = 8, jev_cache_ttl_s = 3600, jev_cache_max_entries = 200. Under [jev.routing]: max_adjustment = 0.25, evidence_floor_n = 10. New tables: [jev.points] scout_necessity = "shadow", context_escalation = "shadow", review_escalation = "shadow", planner_relaunch = "shadow"; [allocation] mode = "shadow", min_samples = 5, latency_weight_usd_per_hour = 2.0, critical_factor = 1.0, non_critical_factor = 0.25; [strategy] mode = "shadow", min_samples = 10; [speculation] mode = "off", min_fix_round_p = 0.5, min_samples = 5, min_retry_cost_usd = 1.0; [promotion] min_samples = 20. Read each module (duration, capacity, concurrency, merge_pressure, jev_sched, jev_route, jev_points, allocation, strategy, speculation, promotion) to confirm the default names and values before writing; if a module's default differs from this list, the module wins and the spec value is corrected in the file with a note in the commit message.
Place the two new [jev.routing] keys AFTER the existing cache_max_entries line (tests/test_jev_route.py::test_pool_toml_jev_routing_table_follows_jev pins cache_max_entries = 500 at a fixed offset from the table header). Prompt files are out of scope for this task: the Planner already committed the prompt rules on main.
Tests (unittest.TestCase methods, tests/test_pool.py, import _harness first): parse .orchestrator/pool.toml with tomllib and assert the listed keys exist with the listed values and that [scheduler].mode and [jev.routing].mode stay "shadow" and [speculation].mode is "off".
acceptance: tests/test_pool.py::test_pool_toml_documents_roadmap_defaults — tomllib parse of .orchestrator/pool.toml yields every listed key with the listed default, [scheduler].mode and [jev.routing].mode shadow, [speculation].mode off
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_pool_toml_jev_routing_table_follows_jev still passes (cache_max_entries keeps its position) and .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

result.summary: Config-only diff. Verified every new pool.toml key/value against the actual DEFAULTS or default-arg in each of the 10 roadmap modules (duration, capacity, concurrency, merge_pressure, jev_sched, jev_route, jev_points, allocation, strategy, speculation, promotion) — all match exactly. jev.routing new keys (max_adjustment, evidence_floor_n) are appended after cache_max_entries, preserving the routing+5 offset pinned by test_jev_route.py::test_pool_toml_jev_routing_table_follows_jev. Ran both named tests locally: both pass. No secrets touched, no code changes, no behavior change.
